 Cardiff City v Burnley halted as players and fans gesture to the stands
 The match at Cardiff City Stadium was stopped late in the game
 Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Glen Williams 16:54, 07 Nov 2026 View Image Cardiff City manager Brian Barry-Murphy
 The Championship match between Cardiff City and Burnley at Cardiff City Stadium was halted on 83 minutes after an incident in the stands.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 Players and fans were seen to be gesturing towards the Ninian Stand, trying to raise the alarm.
 ‌ 
 It is not known what the cause of the stoppage was - although it appears to have been some sort of medical emergency.
 Cardiff manager Brian Barry-Murphy could be seen in conversation with the referee and fourth official as he tried to establish what was happening.
 Two members of the Bluebirds' medical team could be seen making their way to the scene.
 On Cardiff City TV there was obvious concern shown
 ‌ 
 "First and foremost, there's a medical emergency in the Ninian Stand. Football takes a back seat at moments like this, doesn't it?" the commentator said.
 "Absolutely," said the co-commentator. "You never like to see this, of course. People go to a football game for enjoyment, for relaxation. Hopefully this is just precautionary.
 ‌ 
 "Over in the Ninian Stand, as we look across, in fairness, the medical teams and stewards have reacted very quickly.
 "Despite the excitement here at Cardiff City Stadium, football rightly takes a distant second place right now."
 Article continues below The game was stopped for five minutes in total, with the game back under way on 88 minutes.
 More follows.
